error_direction_rationale: The kernel is exact rational arithmetic over caller-declared aggregates with a single declared rounding rule (round half-up at the final step only, integer basis points); it adds no one-sided approximation of its own. Every target is either a pinned published figure carried as a comparison reference (speed, 75 percent within one hour) or declared on the page as a design convention (availability, 99.9 percent reference); misses and meets are reported symmetrically as meets_target, never as a verdict. The honest direction for exact arithmetic with symmetric comparison is undirected.

derived_from.clause_path: FSB Targets for Addressing the Four Challenges of Cross-border Payments, Final Report 13 October 2021 — quantified targets table, speed segment (wholesale and retail rows); retail cost framing
FSB Annual Progress Report methodology document, 2025 update — Table 3 retail segment KPI definitions (cost, speed, access, transparency)
CPMI-IOSCO PFMI April 2012, Principle 17 Operational risk — principle statement (no numeric availability KPI)

branches.clause: FSB 2021 targets table retail speed row: 75% of cross-border retail payments to provide availability of funds within one hour, by end-2027; FSB 2025 methodology Speed KPI 1
branches.branch: Where transactions.count is a non-negative integer and credited_within_1h_count is declared non-negative, speed_pct_within_1h is the declared within-one-hour count over the declared total, half-up to 2 decimal places of percent.

branches.clause: FSB 2021 targets table: the 75-percent-within-one-hour figure is a cross-border retail/wholesale payments target
branches.branch: The speed target attaches only on the g20_retail and fast_payment_scheme profiles; on generic no target is claimed and meets_target is absent.
branches.note: Fixture channel-totals-mismatch-dq-flag (generic profile): speed_pct_within_1h carries no target member.

branches.clause: FSB 2021 speed target remainder clause (within one business day); FSB 2025 methodology Speed KPI 2
branches.branch: Where credited_within_1bd_count is not declared, speed_pct_within_1bd is null with reason_code NOT_DECLARED — never zero and never inferred as the complement of the one-hour share.
branches.note: Fixture fps-month-meets-speed-target: speed_pct_within_1bd null/NOT_DECLARED (only credited_within_1bd_count present in prior-period-deltas-g20 makes it non-null).

branches.clause: FSB 2025 methodology Table 3 retail Cost KPIs 1-4 (average cost of payment transactions); retail cost framing in the 2021 targets table
branches.branch: Where cost.fee_value and transactions.value are declared non-negative, cost_avg_fee_bps is fee value over transaction value in integer basis points.

branches.clause: CPMI-IOSCO PFMI April 2012 Principle 17 statement (operational risk; the principle sets no numeric availability KPI)
branches.branch: Where availability.scheduled_minutes and unplanned_downtime_minutes are declared non-negative, availability_pct is (scheduled minus unplanned downtime) over scheduled, half-up to 2 decimal places of percent; the 99.9 reference level applies only on fast_payment_scheme and gov_payments and is a design convention.

branches.clause: Design convention (declared on the page): no FSB failure-rate or fraud KPI; G20 roadmap monitors complaints qualitatively
branches.branch: failure_rate_bps and fraud_count_share_bps denominate on the declared transaction count; fraud_rate_bps on transaction value; complaints_resolution_pct on complaints.received; each is null with a reason code when its inputs are not declared.

branches.clause: FSB 2025 methodology Table 3 retail Access KPIs 1-2 (transaction-account ownership), adapted per-1000-eligible as a declared design convention
branches.branch: Where adoption.active_users and eligible_population are declared non-negative integers, adoption_users_per_1000_eligible is active users over eligible population scaled by 1000; where adoption is not declared the KPI is null with reason_code NOT_DECLARED.
branches.note: Fixture adoption-missing-null-with-reason: null/NOT_DECLARED for the adoption KPIs.

branches.clause: FSB 2025 methodology Table 3 retail Transparency KPI 1 (PSPs providing expected time to fund delivery, tracking status, terms of service), adapted to cost-and-speed disclosure as a declared design convention
branches.branch: Where transparency.services_total is a non-negative integer and services_disclosing_cost_and_speed is a non-negative integer, transparency_disclosure_pct is the disclosing share, half-up to 2 decimal places of percent.

branches.clause: Design convention: monitoring-report presentation form (FSB annual progress-report style)
branches.branch: Where prior_period of the same aggregate shape is declared, deltas carry current, prior, abs_delta and pct_delta for every KPI non-null on both sides; a prior period that does not compute raises PRIOR_PERIOD_NOT_COMPUTABLE as a data-quality flag.

branches.clause: Declared input contract: profile is one of generic, g20_retail, fast_payment_scheme, gov_payments (closed set)
branches.branch: A profile outside the closed four-value set is refused — the target set and profile notes are profile-keyed and an unknown profile has no defined targets. Never guessed.

branches.clause: Declared input contract: aggregate counts and values only — a string where a number belongs is identifier-like or free text by construction
branches.branch: Any string value in a declared numeric field (transactions, availability, fraud, complaints, adoption, cost, transparency) is refused before coercion; the field name is named in refused_field and the value is never echoed.

branches.clause: Declared input contract: every rate KPI denominates on transactions.count
branches.branch: transactions.count missing or not a non-negative integer is refused — no rate can be computed without its denominator and none is invented.

branches.clause: Declared input contract: declared aggregates are non-negative; a negative declaration is a caller data error, not a zero
branches.branch: Negative declared values do not refuse the whole pack: each affected KPI goes null with reason_code NEGATIVE_INPUT and a NEGATIVE_DECLARED_VALUE data-quality flag names the offending fields.
branches.note: Value, its source, and owner: declared aggregate counts/values, supplied by the operator; the kernel declines to interpret them and reports the defect. Exercised by property test seeded-negative-input (class-A invalid-domain rejection).

assumption_of_use.value: Non-negative declared aggregate counts and values (each affected KPI goes null with NEGATIVE_INPUT rather than being computed from a negative)
assumption_of_use.owner: the calling operator, who owns the declared figures

branches.clause: Design convention: declared channel breakdowns must reconcile to the declared totals (scheme-operations MI hygiene)
branches.branch: Where by_channel is declared, channel count and value sums that disagree with the declared totals raise CHANNEL_COUNT_TOTALS_MISMATCH / CHANNEL_VALUE_TOTALS_MISMATCH data-quality flags; the KPIs still compute from the declared totals, and manual_review_required is true.
branches.note: Fixture channel-totals-mismatch-dq-flag: both mismatch flags fire.

branches.clause: Declared input contract: a credited-within-one-hour count cannot exceed the transaction total it denominates on
branches.branch: credited_within_1h_count (or credited_within_1bd_count) above transactions.count raises CREDITED_WITHIN_1H_ABOVE_TOTAL (resp. 1BD) as a data-quality flag.
branches.note: Declared-exclusion shape: the caller owns declaring internally consistent counts; the kernel flags the inconsistency rather than silently renormalising. Exercised by property test credited-above-total-flagged.

assumption_of_use.value: credited_within_1h_count and credited_within_1bd_count no greater than transactions.count
assumption_of_use.owner: the calling operator, who owns internal consistency of the declared counts

branches.clause: Declared input contract (aggregate only, no PII) per the staging row PAYMENT-SYSTEM-MI-PACK-1; transaction-level records are out of scope by input
branches.branch: The kernel accepts only aggregate scalars and flat per-channel/per-reason counts; it has no field for individual records and never echoes any input value back (refusal payloads name fields, never values).
branches.note: Value, its source, and owner: aggregate-only inputs, owned by the calling operator. Exercised by evidence.pii_carried === false on every observed run.

assumption_of_use.value: Aggregate scalars and flat per-channel/per-reason counts only; no transaction-level records, no personal data
assumption_of_use.source: the declared input schema (aggregate-only by construction)
assumption_of_use.owner: the calling operator, who must not attempt to pass record-level data

branches.clause: Single declared rounding rule: round half-up at the final step only, integer basis points
branches.branch: The tie-at-exactly-half behaviour of the final half-up step is not pinned by a dedicated fixture; the declared error direction on this branch is conservative_toward_no_finding: a tie rounds up, which can only raise a reported percentage and therefore cannot manufacture a target miss that the exact value does not have.
